policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'eighteen cubits' renders the measure with the plural English demands after a numeral, which the qere plural אַמּוֹת and the ketiv singular אמה (the ordinary idiom of a singular noun after a number) both yield identically; no italic supply and no textual note on 25:17. Base qere fallback carries the projection.
